memory.content: Ultimate Hermes↔Grokbot Bridge: Grok→Hermes paths are native HTTP API :8642 (preferred for fleet) and SSH ask-relay (Desktop-primary hosts with no API gateway). Hermes→Grok paths are the local grok-bot-cli / allowlisted wrapper (primary) and a Tailscale-only webhook POST+Bearer fallback. Private net only; never Funnel or public webhook listeners.

Fleet ask and identity fronts: SOLE PATH HTTP :8642 over the private net. Soft “prefer HTTP” wording left an SSH door and caused flakes where bots claimed HTTP then health “magically” worked after SSH confusion. Do not probe SSH when :8642 fails — report BLOCKED on HTTP path; fix Tailscale, ACL grants, or the Hermes API sidecar.

Hermes→Grok webhook inbound must use Tailscale IP or MagicDNS with Bearer routine-key auth. CLI outbound from Hermes to the Grok Bot app uses loopback and does not need Tailscale. Prefer CLI first; webhook is the fallback when the app session is unusable or Hermes is remote.

grok-bot-cli doctor must show a usable Grok Bot app session. AMBIGUOUS_ENTRIES (multiple gateway descriptor entries with none active) blocks sends — recover by signing out/in or selecting one gateway entry. Do not invent alternate gateway credentials.

A Grok Bot Computer Update can wipe installed software and everything outside /home/box, including default Tailscale state. Keep Tailscale state, restore scripts, and configs under /home/box; store a reusable tagged auth key as an injected secret; run an hourly every-day detect-and-restore routine; pass the uninstall drill before calling setup done.

Typical private-net ACL pattern between a controller-tagged Grok Bot node and Hermes-tagged nodes: allow TCP for SSH, Hermes HTTP :8642, and the operator’s webhook port — not allow-all. Prefer MagicDNS over raw IPs.

Never share one messaging bot token across Hermes hosts via fleet-wide vault inject. Store TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN_<PROFILE> (and other per-host credentials as FOO_<PROFILE>) so Hermes auto-aliases per active profile; a generic FOO in the vault silently shadows per-profile keys.

Public Commander’s Intent / Public bot shares pack only the sanitized Tailscale fleet skill with placeholders. Never pack a fleet-private Tailscale topology skill (live IPs, MagicDNS tails, machine names, keys) into create_bot_share_json.

Marketplace references (reconnect after import; custom MCP connectors do not travel inside the template): Hermes API Fleet for :8642 talk, Hermes SSH Relay for Desktop-primary SSH ask, Hermes Fleet Ops for secrets/homogenize. Bridge docs: https://github.com/shagghiesuperstar/hermes-grok-bridge and https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/.

FAIL LOUD always: when any talk path, routine, or restore fails, pauses, stalls, or goes idle, tell the operator immediately in plain language with the reason and which path. Never leave a dead path quiet.
Paste messy SOPs into Hermes SKILL.md via https://paste-to-skill.vercel.app (Hermes flavor) then install under ~/.hermes/skills/<name>/SKILL.md. Client-side only; never paste secrets.

---
name: Ultimate Hermes↔Grokbot bidirectional
description: >-
  Use when wiring or operating any talk path between Grok Bot and Hermes in
  either direction (HTTP :8642, SSH relay, Hermes CLI, Tailscale webhook), or
  when choosing which path to use.
---
# Ultimate Hermes ↔ Grok Bot bidirectional bridge

## What this pack is
One SSOT for **all** talk paths between a Grok Bot computer and Hermes hosts — both directions. Prefer the primary path; keep the documented fallback ready. Never put secrets, keys, or live IPs into templates or chat.

## Direction map

| Direction | Primary | Fallback | Network |
|-----------|---------|----------|---------|
| **Grok → Hermes** | Native HTTP API `:8642` (marketplace: Hermes API Fleet) | SSH ask-relay (marketplace: Hermes SSH Relay) — Desktop-primary / no API gateway only | Private net only (Tailscale or equiv). Never Funnel / public bind |
| **Hermes → Grok** | `gbot` / allowlisted `gbot-hermes` CLI (loopback to local Grok Bot app session) | Tailscale-only webhook (POST + Bearer) into a Grok Bot inbound routine | CLI = loopback (no Tailscale). Webhook = Tailscale IP or MagicDNS only |

Optional last resorts (operator policy): shared file mailbox drops; team chat only when both talk paths are down.

---

## A. Grok Bot → Hermes — HTTP `:8642` (preferred for fleet)

### When
Gateway + API server on Hermes; parallel fleet asks; orchestrator / identity bots.

### Standing lock (fleet)
For fleet ask and identity fronts: **SOLE PATH HTTP `:8642`**. Soft “prefer HTTP” left an SSH door and caused flakes. Do **not** probe SSH when `:8642` fails — report **BLOCKED on HTTP path**; fix Tailscale / grants / API sidecar.

### Wire
1. Hermes: `API_SERVER_ENABLED=true`, strong `API_SERVER_KEY` in a secret store, bind for private reach only.
2. From Grok Bot: curl `http://<tailscale-ip-or-magicdns>:8642/health`, then authenticated `/v1/models`. Expect `mode=http`.
3. Add one marketplace/custom connector per host (`hermes-<hostname>`) with base URL + Bearer from the secret store.
4. MCP / bot instructions: `SOLE PATH HTTP :8642 — SSH RELAY IS FORBIDDEN`. Delete orphan SSH instruction IDs.
5. Smoke tiny `health` / `ask`. Do not write into Hermes memory plugins unless there is an explicit memory plan.

### Docs
- https://github.com/shagghiesuperstar/hermes-grok-bridge (`docs/NATIVE_API.md`)
- https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/
- Companion skills in this pack: method chooser, HTTP-only talk path, Wire Hermes native API.

---

## B. Grok Bot → Hermes — SSH relay (Desktop-primary)

### When
Hermes is Desktop-primary with **no** standing API gateway on `:8642`, or a single-host public installer. **Not** for fleet identity ask when `:8642` exists.

### Wire
1. Private net reach + `ssh -o BatchMode=yes user@host` from the Grok Bot computer.
2. Clone or copy https://github.com/shagghiesuperstar/hermes-grok-bridge `ssh-relay/`.
3. Custom MCP: `python3` → `ssh-relay/src/hermes_grok_relay/server.py` with `HERMES_RELAY_SSH_TARGET`, `HERMES_RELAY_IDENTITY_NAME`; optional identity file / opts / timeout via env (never in the template).
4. Smoke MCP `health`, then trivial `ask`.

### Docs
- `docs/SSH_RELAY.md` in hermes-grok-bridge
- Companion skill: hermes-ssh-relay-setup

---

## C. Hermes → Grok Bot — CLI (primary)

### When
Hermes (or an allowlisted wrapper) must message, list bots, or doctor the Grok Bot gateway from the **same Mac** where Grok Bot.app is signed in.

### Lessons learned
- Install official `grok-bot-cli` (`gbot`) with a Node version meeting the CLI minimum.
- Prefer an allowlisted wrapper (e.g. `~/bin/gbot-hermes`) that default-denies dangerous verbs (`bots delete`, raw approvals, secret patterns) and caps sends. Hermes `command_allowlist` is allow-more, not confine-to — discipline + wrapper, not YOLO alone.
- `gbot doctor` must show a **usable** app session. `AMBIGUOUS_ENTRIES` (multiple gateway descriptor entries, none active) blocks all sends — fix by signing out/in or selecting one gateway entry; never invent alternate credentials.
- CLI outbound uses **loopback**; Tailscale is not required for this leg.
- Never paste gateway tokens into chat. Never set env credential workarounds unless the operator explicitly ordered that recovery.

### Smoke
`gbot doctor` → usable session; `gbot bots list --json` returns a roster (not an error object).

---

## D. Hermes → Grok Bot — webhook fallback

### When
CLI/session is down, Hermes is on another host, or the operator wants push without waiting on the desktop CLI.

### Hard rules
1. **Tailscale-first only** — post to the Grok Bot computer’s Tailscale IP or MagicDNS. **No Funnel, no public URL, no public webhook listener.**
2. Authenticate with a **Bearer routine key** (secret store). Never log or pack the key.
3. Grok Bot side: inbound routine (or receiver) that accepts POST, verifies Bearer, then runs the job. Keep state under `/home/box`.
4. Typical ACL pattern between controller tag and Hermes tag: TCP for SSH, `:8642`, and the webhook port the operator chose — tighten, don’t open `*→*`.
5. Grok replies still go through `:8642`, mailbox, shared memory bank, or the ticket system — not by opening a public reverse path.

### Smoke
From a Hermes host on the tailnet: authenticated POST → routine wakes → bot ACKs on an agreed channel (mailbox file or `:8642` ask). Silent failure = FAIL LOUD.

---

## E. Shared prerequisites (both directions)

### Private net / Tailscale
- Grok Bot computer must be a Tailscale node for `:8642` and webhook legs.
- **Computer Update wipes everything outside `/home/box`** (including default Tailscale state in `/var/lib`). Keep state, restore scripts, and configs under `/home/box`; reusable tagged auth key as an injected secret; hourly detect-and-restore routine; pass the uninstall drill. Skill: Grok Bot computer update survival (Tailscale).
- Public templates pack only sanitized Tailscale skill (placeholders). Never pack fleet-private topology skills into a Public share.

### Fail loud
If any path dies, pauses, or goes idle: tell the operator immediately with the reason and which path. Do not soft-fallback fleet ask to SSH. Do not pretend health is OK when mode is wrong.

### Secrets
Never commit or chat-paste: `API_SERVER_KEY`, SSH private keys, webhook Bearer, Tailscale auth keys, gateway tokens, messaging bot tokens. Per-host messaging tokens use `FOO_<PROFILE>` vault keys only (see messaging-token isolation skill).

### Method chooser (quick)
1. Need fleet / parallel / identity ask → **HTTP `:8642`**.
2. Desktop-primary Hermes, no API → **SSH relay**.
3. Hermes pushing to Grok on same Mac → **CLI**.
4. Hermes pushing when CLI/session broken or remote → **Tailscale webhook**.
5. Both broken → mailbox / operator chat (policy), then repair primary paths.

---

## References
- Bridge repo: https://github.com/shagghiesuperstar/hermes-grok-bridge
- Hermes docs: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/
- Marketplace templates: **Hermes API Fleet** (HTTP), **Hermes SSH Relay** (SSH), **Hermes Fleet Ops** (secrets/homogenize — talk path still HTTP-only for fleet)
- Paste messy SOPs into Hermes skills: https://paste-to-skill.vercel.app (Hermes flavor)
- Public Tailscale skill: Tailscale fleet macOS (sanitized placeholders only)

# Getting started — Hermes ↔ Grok Bot bridge

You are the **Ultimate Hermes↔Grokbot Bridge** pack. Your job is to wire and operate bi-directional talk between the owner's Grok Bot computer and their Hermes hosts.

Ask **one question at a time**. After each answer, write a short memory (job/convention only — no secrets). When setup is enough to smoke-test, do the smokes and report PASS/BLOCKED plainly.

## First line
Tell the owner: you pack Grok→Hermes (HTTP `:8642` + SSH relay) and Hermes→Grok (CLI + Tailscale webhook fallback), private-net only.

## Questions (in order)
1. **What should I be called?** (save as your name if they want a rename)
2. **How many Hermes hosts**, and does each already expose the native API on port **8642** over Tailscale (or equivalent private net)?
3. **Preferred Grok→Hermes path:** fleet HTTP `:8642`, Desktop-primary SSH relay, or both documented with HTTP primary?
4. **Hermes→Grok:** is the Grok Bot app signed in on the same Mac as Hermes (CLI), or do they need the **Tailscale webhook** fallback (or both)?
5. **Connectors / marketplace:** install Hermes API Fleet and/or Hermes SSH Relay templates as needed; confirm Tailscale (or private net) is up on the Grok Bot computer. Custom MCP connectors cannot travel inside this template — they reconnect after import.
6. **Secrets:** confirm API keys, SSH identity, webhook Bearer, and Tailscale auth keys live in a secret store or injected secrets — never paste them into chat. Offer the secure secret request when a key is missing.
7. **Survival:** if this runs on a Grok Bot computer that can be Computer-Updated, confirm Tailscale state + restore scripts live under `/home/box` and an hourly detect-restore routine exists (or create one from the survival skill).

## After answers
1. Load the Ultimate Hermes↔Grokbot bidirectional skill and pick paths from the method chooser.
2. Smoke Grok→Hermes: `health` on `:8642` **or** SSH relay `health`/`ask`.
3. Smoke Hermes→Grok: `gbot doctor` usable session **or** authenticated Tailscale webhook POST.
4. FAIL LOUD on any block — name the path and the fix (Tailscale, grants, API sidecar, AMBIGUOUS_ENTRIES session, missing secret). Never soft-fallback fleet ask to SSH.

## Never
- Pack or echo secrets
- Open Funnel / public webhooks
- Use fleet-private Tailscale topology skills in a Public re-share
- Claim a path works without a smoke

---
# Hermes HTTP-only talk path

## When to use
Any ask/health/manage of fleet Hermes (fleet identity hosts when wired), or when connector prompts / MCP instructions still mention SSH.

## Standing lock
**SOLE PATH:** HTTP API `:8642` over Tailscale via one `hermes-<hostname>` connector per host.
**SSH relay to Hermes is FORBIDDEN** for identity bots and the fleet orchestrator ask/manage. Not “prefer HTTP” — there is no SSH door.

## Symptom this killed
Bots said “HTTP API” then health “magically” became ok. Cause: live connectors already spoke HTTP `:8642`, but stale MCP custom instructions still labeled old server IDs as SSH, and soft prompts left an SSH option.

## Hard-kill checklist
1. Delete orphan SSH instruction IDs.
2. Rewrite named + live-ID MCP instructions to: `SOLE PATH HTTP :8642 — SSH RELAY IS FORBIDDEN`.
3. Update host identity prompts the same way.
4. Fleet orchestrator: Hermes talk = HTTP only; SSH only for rare host surgery after API is proven insufficient.
5. Backup config before edits.
6. Verify: `health` → `mode=http`, ok; instructions start with SOLE PATH…

## Keep the path alive
- Computer Update wipes Tailscale outside `/home/box` — use the survival skill + hourly restore.
- Tailscale grants must allow `tcp:8642`.
- Connect-then-reset on `:8642` means Hermes API is dead, not the network.

## Never
- Probe SSH when `:8642` flakes
- Soft-fallback to SSH ask — report BLOCKED on HTTP path
- Soft “prefer HTTP” wording
- Secrets in chat or template packs

## Docs
- https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/
- https://github.com/shagghiesuperstar/hermes-grok-bridge

skills.name: Grok Bot computer update survival (Tailscale)
skills.description: Use this when setting up Tailscale (or any installed tool, daemon, or key) on the Grok Bot computer, when the computer may have been updated or reset, or when the bot can't reach tailnet hosts. It makes the setup survive a Computer Update and restore itself with no human step.
skills.content:
---
name: Grok Bot computer update survival (Tailscale)
description: >-
  Use this when setting up Tailscale (or any installed tool, daemon, or key) on
  the Grok Bot computer, when the computer may have been updated or reset, or
  when the bot can't reach tailnet hosts. It makes the setup survive a Computer
  Update and restore itself with no human step.
---
# Grok Bot computer update survival (Tailscale)

## Why
The Grok Bot computer can be moved to a fresh instance (Computer Update) at any time. Installed software, daemons, and everything outside `/home/box` are wiped. Injected secrets and `/home/box` survive. Tailscale’s default state in `/var/lib/tailscale` is lost on every update.

**Rule:** never leave state, keys, configs, or scripts outside `/home/box`. Anything installed needs a restore script under `/home/box` plus an automatic check.

## One-time setup
1. Persistent folder e.g. `/home/box/agent-data/infra/` with `scripts/` and `tailscale-state/`.
2. Mint a reusable tagged auth key in Tailscale admin; if Tailnet Lock is on, pre-sign it. Never put Lock signing keys on the Grok Bot computer.
3. Store key as injected secret `TAILSCALE_AUTHKEY_SIGNED` via secure secret request — never paste into chat.
4. Start `tailscaled` with `--state` and `--statedir` under the persistent folder; then `tailscale up` with the auth key and advertise tags.
5. Save idempotent `scripts/restore-tailscale.sh` (install if missing, start daemon, fast-path if Running, else `tailscale up`; exit 10 NEED_SECRET / 20 NEED_LOCK_SIGNATURE).
6. Save `scripts/detect-fresh-box.sh` (exit 0 when restore needed).
7. Create hourly every-day routine: detect → restore → FAIL LOUD on NEED_SECRET / NEED_LOCK_SIGNATURE; silent when healthy.

## Prove it (drill)
Record IP → kill tailscaled + remove package → detect → restore → IP must match; lock signed; known host answers.

## Checklist before calling setup done
Everything under `/home/box`? Automatic restore? Drill passed? If any no, say so plainly.

  PUBLIC SANITIZED. Use for Public templates and Tailscale recovery with

  keys.
---
# Tailscale fleet (PUBLIC SANITIZED)

> Placeholders only. Never pack fleet-private topology into a Public share.

## When
Any Tailscale CLI, admin console, Tailnet Lock, MagicDNS, ACL tags, node key expiry, or Tailscale SSH between fleet nodes.

## Topology (Owner fills)
| Role | Placeholder | Tag |
|---|---|---|
| Hermes nodes | `<NODE_*>.<TAILNET_MAGICDNS>` | `<TAG_HERMES_NODE>` |
| Grok Bot controller | `<NODE_CONTROLLER>` | `<TAG_CONTROLLER>` |

Prefer MagicDNS. Example ACL: controller → Hermes TCP for SSH, `:8642`, and webhook port — not allow-all.

## Variants (macOS)
Detect first. Never run Standalone and App Store together. App Store lacks Tailscale SSH — use Standalone for fleet SSH.

## Key expiry / Lock
`tailscale status` + `tailscale lock status`. Never put Lock signing keys on the Grok Bot computer. Never logout the last signing node.

## Diagnostics
`tailscale ping`, `tailscale netcheck`. Connect-timeout → Tailscale/ACL; connect-then-reset on `:8642` → Hermes API dead.

## Never
Paste auth keys in chat. Don’t claim recovery without status + lock + real ping.

name: hermes-fleet-messaging-token-isolation
description: >-
  use this when documenting Hermes fleet Bitwarden secrets for messaging bots or

---
# Hermes fleet messaging token isolation

## When
Setting up Bitwarden Secrets Manager (or any bulk secret source) across multiple Hermes hosts/profiles that use Telegram/Discord/Slack bots, or any credential that must differ per host.

## Hard rule
**Never store a single shared `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` in a fleet-wide vault project that every host pulls with `override_existing: true`.** That makes every gateway the same bot → Conflict → cross-wired DMs/crons.

## Correct pattern
Vault keys: `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN_<PROFILE>` (profile uppercased, `-` → `_`). Hermes auto-aliases to `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` for the active profile. Same for other credential-shaped names ending in `_API_KEY`, `_TOKEN`, `_SECRET`, `_KEY`, or `_PASSWORD`.

**An alias never shadows a variable supplied under its real name.** If generic `FOO` also exists in the vault, per-profile entries are silently ignored. For per-host credentials store only `FOO_<PROFILE>` — never a generic `FOO`.

## Checklist
1. One messaging bot per identity/host.
2. Store per-profile keys only.
3. Confirm gateway log applies profile-scoped token.
4. Smoke getMe matches intended bot; no Conflict.
5. Only one process polls a given token.
6. Vault has no bare generic entry for that name.

## Recovery
Fingerprint live bots via getMe (never print tokens) → restore correct tokens → delete shared vault generic key → clear cache → restart → re-verify.
